x: Against the computer, a new switch under the strength: Training. Turn it on before the game and you can take back a move as often as you like. A training game counts for neither your Elo nor your badges; switched off, the game is rated and nothing helps you.

t: After a boss, the next chapter
x: When your game against a boss ends, the card on the board now offers what comes next: the next chapter once you have won, or another try. After the last boss, puzzles or a game.

Fourteen new badges: one for each chapter you finish (chapters 2 to 9), three for the bosses, one for the whole path and two for the placement test. What you have already done counts: those badges are waiting in your collection.

t: Your games between members, time control by time control
x: In Statistics, your games between members now show won, drawn and lost for each time control: Blitz, Rapid, Classical, Correspondence. Tap a time control to see its bar. Your total stays as it is; the detail starts counting with the games you play from today.

t: The boss opens the next chapter, and matching time controls
x: In Learn, beating a chapter's boss now opens the next chapter. After three losses against it, the next chapter opens anyway, and the chapters you had already opened stay open. Between members, time controls now match the ones against the computer: 5+3 is a Blitz, and Rapid gains 10+5.

t: Clearer statistics, a simpler Against a friend screen
x: Your statistics are now grouped by category, and members get a won, drawn, lost bar. The Against a friend screen fits in one block: pick a time control, from Blitz to correspondence, then invite. And a square at the bottom right tells you when a game is waiting for you.

t: The learning path is complete: six new chapters
x: Six chapters join the Learn tab: The checkmates to know, Double threats, Pins and skewers, Starting a game well, Basic endgames, Mate in two. The path now has nine chapters, from your very first moves to mate in two.

t: A Learn tab, with a path to follow
x: The new Learn tab gathers everything you need to get started: a path of chapters made of short lessons on the board, each ending with a boss, the computer playing with a handicap. "I'm a beginner" becomes chapter 1 and your progress is kept; two new chapters follow, All the rules and Give nothing away. A placement test can choose your starting chapter, your puzzle level and the computer's strength. The rule sheets have moved there from Explore.

t: A coach to review your games
x: After a game, run the review: for each blunder or mistake, the coach tells you why in one sentence ("the bishop on g5 was attacked and nothing defends it") and shows the move it recommends. Positions where one move was clearly better join your Mistakes to review, so you can replay them. Free, with no limit.

"Challenge a friend" is now called Puzzle duel, and your puzzle score is now your Puzzle rating, so you no longer mix it up with your Elo. Puzzles in a duel count toward your daily goal, but they move neither your puzzle rating nor your level.

t: New badges for games between members
x: Your games against other members now have their badges: first game, first point, Blitz, correspondence, random opponent, Elo milestones. There are also badges for your Elo against the computer, friends, puzzle duels and leagues. The ones you had already earned are in your collection.

t: An Elo for each kind of game between members
x: Between members, Blitz, Rapid, Classical and Correspondence games now each have their own Elo. The Elo you already had becomes your Rapid Elo. When you start another kind of game, you begin from your Rapid Elo. All four are on your player card and in My progress.

t: Moves prepared in advance, and arrows
x: While your opponent is thinking, you can already play your next moves: each one is made as soon as it is your turn, if it is still allowed. Tap anywhere else to cancel them. On a computer, a right-click draws arrows and circles on the board, for your eyes only.
A faster live time control: 3 minutes each, plus 2 seconds added after every move. In Play, Against a friend or Against a player online, under Blitz.

Members can now play by correspondence: each player has 1, 3 or 7 days for every move, and the game waits on the site. Invite a friend by username or find an opponent close to your level; your games in progress are listed at the top of Play.
Members can now play live, with a clock kept by the server: invite a friend by username or by link, or find an opponent close to your level. In Play, on the Against a friend card.
Moves now show the pieces of the board instead of English letters: the knight is drawn rather than written N, in every language. Copied as PGN, a game keeps the letters every chess program reads.

At the Beginner and Casual levels, the computer no longer gives away its queen at random: it makes the kind of mistakes a player of its level makes. It also takes a moment to think before moving. And the explanations under the puzzles have been checked one by one by Stockfish.
The bright yellow gives way to a soft copper on a blue-grey background. The opening, endgame and glossary pages turn dark too, like the rest of the site. The themes you earn do not change.
Play now opens on two cards: against the computer or against a friend. Every card on the site has its own pictogram. The transfer code and the progress reset have moved to the menu.

Five leagues, from Pawn to Queen. Each week you play in a group of about 20 players, ranked by puzzles solved: the top 5 move up, the bottom 5 move down. They open once 50 players are active in the same week. Follow the count in My league, under Top players, with a free account.

Your badge collection, your progress charts, the themes you have earned and your full game history now open with a free account. Everything you play stays free without one, and nothing you have earned is lost.

For members: creating an account, inviting a member to a puzzle duel, adding a friend, reaching a top 10, giving your opinion. For everyone: three badges for puzzle duels between friends, including a perfect five out of five.

t: A leaderboard just for you and your friends
x: Open a player's profile and add them to your friends: you will find them in My friends, under Top players. Nobody is notified, and only you can see your list.
In Top players, tap a username to see that player's profile and invite them to a puzzle duel. Not in the top 50 yet? Your rank now shows under each list.

t: Puzzle duel links show the score to beat
x: When you send a puzzle duel link, its preview now shows your score. Puzzle duel puzzles count toward your daily goal, not your puzzle rating.
Each of the five endgame pages now replays a model game move by move, bishop and knight included.

t: All the stats at a glance
x: In Top players, turn your phone sideways to see every stat of every player and sort by any column.
It now starts its games like a human: Italian, Sicilian, Queen's Gambit and many more, and not the same one every time.

t: Invite a member to a puzzle duel
x: After your five puzzles, send the duel to a member by username. They find it in Menu, Member duels, and you both see the result.

t: A free account, if you want one
x: A username and a code are enough to find your progress on all your devices. Optional: everything still works without one. Menu, My account.
Six leaderboards for players with an account: this week, puzzle rating, puzzles solved, streak, badges and Sprint.
The app now reacts with a wink: the computer scratches its head, the king packs his bags. Several versions take turns, so you won't read the same line twice in a row.
Six themes to earn at their time of year, from the holidays to Songkran: play one day in the period and the theme is yours for good.
Eight new looks for the whole site, from Ice to Gold, each unlocked by a badge. Choose yours in Preferences.
Twenty-two new badges for the openings you play and the traps you set or fall into, from the Italian Game to Scholar's mate. Each one links to its page.
Five puzzles at your level, then a link to send. Your friend plays the same ones and you see who did better. In Solve.
Three new challenges every Monday, the same for everyone. Complete all three for a perfect week and a streak freeze.
A ring fills with each puzzle you solve. Reach your goal 7 days in a row and earn a freeze that saves your streak if you miss a day.
Bronze, silver, gold and jade medals, each with a chess story. Tap a medal to read it.
Your statistics, your badges, the settings and the languages are all gathered here.
Tabs slide, the logo winks, the elephant jumps when you solve a puzzle, and every screen has its sounds.

t: The puzzle of the day on your website
x: Clubs and teachers can show the puzzle of the day on their own website.
Seven steps to learn how the pieces move, checkmate and the first tactics, then play your first game.
Moves, captures, checks and game endings can now be heard. You can turn them off in the preferences.
Italian, Turkish, Polish and Indonesian join the site. And a little Thai secret is hiding on the home page…
The puzzle of the day is easy on Monday and gets tougher until Sunday.
The puzzle bank grows, and the site now speaks Spanish, Portuguese, German and Russian.
